--- pagetitle: "Dingo Tutorial" jupyter: python3 --- ## {.title-dingo} ![](images/dingo.png){.absolute top=90 right=70 width=700} ::: {.absolute top=430 left=100} [[Dingo]{.sc} Tutorial]{.big-title}\ [Usage and code structure]{.big-sub} ::: ::: {.absolute bottom=80 left=100} [Stephen Green]{.byline}\ [with Cecilia Fabbri, Matt Mould, and Lorenzo Pompili]{.coauthors}\ [CCA, Flatiron Institute — 13 November 2026]{.team} ::: ## Introduction [Neural posterior estimation (NPE)]{.sub} ::: {.body} - [Dingo]{.sc} uses neural posterior estimation for gravitational wave inference: 1. Train a neural conditional density estimator to represent the posterior. ![](images/npe_diagram.png){width=1150 style="margin: 10px 0 0 60px;"} 2. Amortized inference: Draw samples $\theta \sim q_\phi(\theta \mid d, S_\text{n})$ for any observed $(d, S_\text{n})$. ::: ## Introduction [References]{.sub} ::: {.body} ::: {.grid2 .even} ::: {.subheads} - [Documentation]{.accent} - - [Code]{.accent} - - Available as `dingo-gw` package from `pip` and `conda`. - [Community Discord server]{.accent} ![](images/discord_qr.svg){width=190 style="margin: 4px 0 0 34px;"}\ [discord.gg/NxzMStfWX](https://discord.gg/NxzMStfWX) ::: ::: {.subheads} - [Leverages Bilby components]{.accent} - Priors, detector information, bilby_pipe automation - [Key papers]{.accent} 1. [arXiv:2002.07656](https://arxiv.org/abs/2002.07656): 5D toy model with normalizing flows 2. [arXiv:2106.12594](https://arxiv.org/abs/2106.12594): Amortized inference with noise conditioning 3. [arXiv:2210.05686](https://arxiv.org/abs/2210.05686): Importance sampling 4. [arXiv:2305.17161](https://arxiv.org/abs/2305.17161): Flow matching 5. [arXiv:2407.09602](https://arxiv.org/abs/2407.09602): Binary neutron stars 6. [arXiv:2512.02968](https://arxiv.org/abs/2512.02968): Transformers ([Dingo]{.sc}-T1) ::: ::: ::: ## Introduction [Key steps]{.sub} ::: {.body} ::: {.steps} ::: {.s1} 1. [Generate training datasets]{.green} a. Intrinsic waveforms (polarizations), specified by masses, spins, inclination, and phase. b. Noise power spectral densities, with a distribution often corresponding to an observing run. ::: ::: {.s2} 2. [Train the network]{.orange} a. Construct network based on specified configuration. b. During training, sample extrinsic parameters (sky position, distance, time of coalescence) and noise realizations, and construct simulated data. ::: ::: {.s3} 3. [Perform inference]{.sblue} a. For (observed or simulated) data, draw posterior samples from the trained network. b. Optionally importance sample to true posterior. Gives Bayesian evidence. ::: ::: {.b1} Specified by YAML config files ::: ::: {.b2} Use [Dingo]{.sc} API or INI file ::: ::: ::: ## Interactive tutorial [Follow along: ]{.sub style="font-size: 36px;"} ::: {.body} ::: {.grid2 .wide-left} ::: {} ::: {.darcula .shell} ```bash git clone https://github.com/stephengreen/dingo-tutorial cd dingo-tutorial uv sync uv run jupyter lab DINGO_Tutorial.ipynb ``` ::: ::: {.compact style="margin-top: 36px;"} - [uv](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/) installs the versions `dingo-gw` 0.10.3 was tested with, and fetches Python 3.12 if needed. Without uv: `pip` with `constraints.txt` (see README). - Section 6 downloads the [Dingo]{.sc}-T1 model (641 MB) from Zenodo: start early. - Notebook by Annalena Kofler, updated for `dingo-gw` 0.10.3. ::: ::: ::: {} ![](images/tutorial_qr.svg){width=360} ::: ::: ::: ## Generating training data [Waveform Dataset]{.sub} ::: {.body} ::: {.grid2} ::: {} - YAML file components: - Domain (f_min, f_max, etc.) - Waveform generator (approximant, etc.) - Intrinsic prior (Bilby format) - Size of dataset - Compression - `dingo_generate_dataset` → HDF5 file. ::: ::: {.panel} [examples/npe_model/waveform_dataset_settings.yaml]{.filetab} ::: {.darcula .sm} ```yaml domain: type: UniformFrequencyDomain f_min: 20.0 f_max: 1024.0 delta_f: 0.125 waveform_generator: approximant: IMRPhenomXPHM # SEOBNRv4PHM f_ref: 20.0 spin_conversion_phase: 0.0 intrinsic_prior: mass_1: bilby.core.prior.Constraint(minimum=10.0, maximum… mass_2: bilby.core.prior.Constraint(minimum=10.0, maximum… chirp_mass: bilby.gw.prior.UniformInComponentsChirpMass(m… mass_ratio: bilby.gw.prior.UniformInComponentsMassRatio(m… phase: default chi_1: bilby.gw.prior.AlignedSpin(name='chi_1', a_prior=U… chi_2: bilby.gw.prior.AlignedSpin(name='chi_2', a_prior=U… theta_jn: default luminosity_distance: 100.0 # Mpc geocent_time: 0.0 # s num_samples: 5000000 compression: svd: size: 200 num_training_samples: 50000 num_validation_samples: 10000 whitening: aLIGO_ZERO_DET_high_P_asd.txt ``` ::: ::: ::: ::: ## Waveform dataset [Multi-banding]{.sub} ::: {.body} ::: {.grid2 .even} ::: {.jup} ::: {#711f803c .cell execution_count=8} ``` {.python .cell-code} from dingo.gw.domains import (UniformFrequencyDomain, MultibandedFrequencyDomain) from dingo.gw.waveform_generator import WaveformGenerator nodes = [20.0, 26.0, 34.0, 46.0, 62.0, 78.0, 1038.0] ufd = UniformFrequencyDomain(f_min=20.0, f_max=nodes[-1], delta_f=1/16) mfd = MultibandedFrequencyDomain(nodes, delta_f_initial=1/16, base_domain=ufd) len(ufd), len(mfd) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=8} ``` (16609, 736) ``` ::: ::: ::: {#be906bd1 .cell execution_count=9} ``` {.python .cell-code} p = dict(chirp_mass=30.0, mass_ratio=0.8, a_1=0.3, a_2=0.2, tilt_1=1.0, tilt_2=2.0, phi_12=1.0, phi_jl=0.5, theta_jn=1.0, phase=0.0, luminosity_distance=100.0, geocent_time=0.0) wfg = WaveformGenerator("IMRPhenomXPHM", ufd, 20.0) wf_ufd = wfg.generate_hplus_hcross(p) wfg = WaveformGenerator("IMRPhenomXPHM", mfd, 20.0) wf_mfd = wfg.generate_hplus_hcross(p) ``` ::: ::: ::: {} ::: {.jup} ::: {#a0ec648f .cell fig-dpi='110' fig-height='6.6' fig-width='7.4' execution_count=10} ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display} ![](index_files/figure-revealjs/cell-11-output-1.png){width=687 height=581} ::: ::: ::: [$\Delta f$ doubles in each band: 16,609 → 736 bins. For a dataset: `dingo_generate_multibanded_domain`.]{.caption} ::: ::: ::: ## Generating training data [ASD Dataset]{.sub} ::: {.body} ::: {.grid2} ::: {} - Executed with `dingo_generate_asd_dataset` - Downloads LVK data from GWOSC and generates PSDs using Welch method. - Key parameters: - Observing run - Set of detectors - Time between PSDs / max number of PSDs ::: ::: {.panel} [examples/npe_model/asd_dataset_settings.yaml]{.filetab} ::: {.darcula .sm} ```yaml dataset_settings: f_s: 4096 time_psd: 1024 T: 8.0 window: roll_off: 0.4 type: tukey time_gap: 0 num_psds_max: 0 detectors: - H1 - L1 observing_run: O1 ``` ::: ::: ::: ::: ## Training [Overview]{.sub} ::: {.body} ::: {.grid2 .even} ::: {} - Training carried out using `dingo_train` (or `dingo_train_condor`) - YAML config file specifies further [data settings]{.green}, [neural network configuration]{.orange}, [training plan]{.sblue}, and additional [local settings]{.accent} (e.g., number of cores, GPUs). - Produces regular checkpoint files (`.pt`), as well as training history information. - Multi-GPU training: set `num_gpus` in local settings. ::: ::: {.panel} [examples/npe_model/train_settings.yaml]{.filetab .s-data} ::: {.darcula .sm} ```yaml data: waveform_dataset_path: training_data/waveform_dataset.hdf5 train_fraction: 0.95 domain_update: f_min: 20.0 f_max: 1024.0 svd_size_update: 200 detectors: [H1, L1] extrinsic_prior: # Sampled at train time dec: default ra: default geocent_time: bilby.core.prior.Uniform(minimum=-0.10, m… psi: default luminosity_distance: bilby.core.prior.Uniform(minimum=1… ref_time: 1126259462.391 inference_parameters: [chirp_mass, mass_ratio, chi_1, chi… theta_jn, dec, ra, geocent_time, luminosity_distance, psi] ``` ::: ::: ::: ::: ## Training [Network configuration]{.sub} ::: {.body} ::: {.grid2} ::: {} - Specifies architecture and size of the NN - Currently supported: spline flows, flow matching, score matching - Embedding network: `resnet` (first layer is initialized with SVD, computed automatically) or `transformer` ([Dingo]{.sc}-T1) - Extension to new architectures is straightforward (requires modification of [Dingo]{.sc} code) ::: ::: {.panel} [examples/npe_model/train_settings.yaml]{.filetab .s-model} ::: {.darcula .sm} ```yaml model: posterior_model_type: normalizing_flow posterior_kwargs: num_flow_steps: 30 base_transform_kwargs: hidden_dim: 1024 num_transform_blocks: 5 activation: elu dropout_probability: 0.0 norm: BatchNorm num_bins: 8 base_transform_type: rq-coupling embedding_type: resnet embedding_kwargs: output_dim: 128 hidden_dims: [1024, 1024, 1024, 1024, 1024, 1024, 512, 512, 512, 512, 512, 512, 256, 256, 256, 256, 256, 256, 128, 128, 128, 128, 128, 128] activation: elu dropout: 0.0 norm: BatchNorm svd: num_training_samples: 50000 num_validation_samples: 10000 size: 200 ``` ::: ::: ::: ::: ## Training [Training plan]{.sub} ::: {.body} ::: {.grid2} ::: {} - Specifies training configuration (epochs, batch size, optimizer, learning rate schedule) - Training stages - **Stage 0**: use fixed ASD per detector. - **Stage 1**: use multiple ASDs per detector.\ → ASDs could cover an entire observing run\ → Learning rate should be reduced (~0.1x) - Training stages may also be used without changing the ASD dataset ::: ::: {.panel} [examples/npe_model/train_settings.yaml]{.filetab .s-training} ::: {.darcula .sm} ```yaml training: stage_0: epochs: 300 asd_dataset_path: training_data/asd_dataset_fiducial/as… freeze_rb_layer: True optimizer: type: adam lr: 5.0e-5 scheduler: type: cosine T_max: 300 batch_size: 4096 stage_1: epochs: 150 asd_dataset_path: training_data/asd_dataset/asds_O1.hdf5 freeze_rb_layer: False optimizer: type: adam lr: 1.0e-5 scheduler: type: cosine T_max: 150 batch_size: 4096 ``` ::: ::: ::: ::: ## Inference [Overview]{.sub} ::: {.body .center .large} - Trained networks for common configurations are on Zenodo (e.g., [Dingo]{.sc}-T1 for O3). - Two options for inference: - **Sampler API** — useful for injections, experiments - **dingo_pipe** — based on bilby_pipe - After inference, typically importance sample to true posterior (default in dingo_pipe). ::: ## Inference [Sampler API]{.sub} ::: {.body} ::: {.grid2 .wide-left} ::: {.jup} ::: {#459700ab .cell execution_count=11} ``` {.python .cell-code} from dingo.core.posterior_models import build_model_from_kwargs from dingo.gw.inference.sampler import GWComposedSampler from dingo.gw.injection import Injection from dingo.gw.noise.asd_dataset import ASDDataset model = build_model_from_kwargs(filename="02_training/model_latest.pt", device="cpu", load_training_info=False) injection = Injection.from_posterior_model_metadata(model.metadata) injection.asd = ASDDataset("01_training_data/asd_dataset/asd_GW150914.hdf5", ifos=["H1", "L1"]) theta = injection.prior.sample() # Random injection from prior. strain_data = injection.injection(theta) # dict sampler = GWComposedSampler.from_model(model, strain_data) sampler.run_sampler(num_samples=10_000, batch_size=5_000) sampler.samples ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=11} ```{=html}

``` ::: ::: ::: ::: ::: ## Inference {visibility="hidden"} ![](images/keynote_slide14.png){.absolute top=0 left=0 width=1920 height=1080} ## Inference [`dingo_pipe`]{.sub} ::: {.body} ::: {.grid2 .text-heavy} ::: {.compact} - Automates inference tasks, including downloading of GW data. Specified by INI file: - **Job submission** - **Sampler:** specify [Dingo]{.sc} models, number of samples, GNPE iterations (Gibbs sampling over detector time shifts), data/prior updates for importance sampling, … - **Data generation:** specify GPS time, point to frame files (or gwosc), point to PSDs. [Dingo]{.sc}-T1: choose detectors, frequency range, PSD notches. - Optional: **injections**, **calibration marginalization** (with importance sampling), **corner and diagnostic plots** - Importance sampling (incl. synthetic phase) runs by default. - Saves a Result HDF5 file in the end, which can also be read by PESummary. ::: ::: {} [Most settings (detectors, etc.) are taken from the [Dingo]{.sc} model.]{.tag} ::: {.panel} [examples/npe_model/GW150914.ini]{.filetab} ::: {.darcula .sm} ```ini local = True request-cpus-importance-sampling = 64 sampling-requirements = [TARGET.CUDAGlobalMemoryMb>40000] model = training/model_latest.pt device = 'cuda' num-samples = 50000 batch-size = 50000 recover-log-prob = true prior-dict-updates = { luminosity_distance = bilby.gw.prior.UniformComovingVolume(… } trigger-time = GW150914 label = GW150914 outdir = outdir_GW150914 channel-dict = {H1:GWOSC, L1:GWOSC} psd-length = 128 plot-corner = true plot-weights = true plot-log-probs = true ``` ::: ::: ::: ::: ::: ## New features {visibility="hidden"} ![](images/keynote_slide16.png){.absolute top=0 left=0 width=1920 height=1080} ## Recent developments [Sampling chains: `GWComposedSampler`]{.sub} ::: {.body} ::: {.grid2 .even} ::: {.compact} - The posterior is an ordered product of conditionals, $$q(\theta \mid d) = \prod_i q_i(\theta_i \mid \theta_{= f_max_lower ``` ::: ::: ::: ::: ::: ## Recent developments [[Dingo]{.sc}-T1: transformer model]{.sub} ::: {.body} ::: {.grid2 .even} ::: {.compact} - Data in each detector are split into **tokens** (16 frequency bins) and processed by a transformer encoder. - Trained with random masking of detectors, frequency ranges, and narrow bands. - A single network analyzes any subset of H1, L1, V1, with per-detector frequency ranges and PSD notches, **without retraining**. - Trained for O3 (IMRPhenomXPHM); available on Zenodo. - Kofler et al., [arXiv:2512.02968](https://arxiv.org/abs/2512.02968) ::: ::: {} ::: {#31519d51 .cell fig-dpi='110' fig-height='6.8' fig-width='7.6' execution_count=15} ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display} ![](index_files/figure-revealjs/cell-16-output-1.png){width=585 height=597} ::: ::: [GW190701_203306, analyzed by the same network with H1 only and with H1 + L1. Bottom: sky position (importance-resampled samples).]{.caption} ::: ::: ::: ## Recent developments [[Dingo]{.sc}-T1: configuration]{.sub} ::: {.body} ::: {.grid2 .even} ::: {} ::: {.compact} - **Training**: `embedding_type: transformer` and a `tokenization` block in the data settings, which sets the masking during training. - **Inference**: per event, in the INI file. Ranges must lie within those seen in training. ::: ::: {.panel style="margin-top: 40px;"} [examples/dingo_t1/GW150914.ini [(excerpt)]{.note}]{.filetab} ::: {.darcula .sm} ```ini channel-dict = {H1:GWOSC, L1:GWOSC} minimum-frequency = {H1: 20, L1: 20} maximum-frequency = {H1: 1024, L1: 1024} psd-notch-dict = {H1: [[59.0, 61.0], [119.0, 121.0]], L1: [… ``` ::: ::: ::: ::: {.panel} [examples/dingo_t1/train_settings.yaml]{.filetab .s-data} ::: {.darcula .sm} ```yaml data: ... tokenization: token_size: 16 normalize_position: true mask_detectors: p_num_masked: [0.6, 0.3, 0.1] p_detector: H1: 0.3 L1: 0.3 V1: 0.4 mask_frequency_range: p_mask: 0.2 f_min_upper: 100.0 f_max_lower: 800.0 p_lower_upper_both: [0.4, 0.4, 0.2] p_same_all_detectors: 0.7 mask_frequency_notches: p_per_detector: 0.3 max_width: 10.0 ``` ::: ::: ::: ::: ## Recent developments [Binary neutron stars]{.sub} ::: {.body} ::: {.grid2 .even} ::: {.compact} - Long inspirals → fine frequency resolution, large data. Chirp mass $\mathcal{M}$ is measured very precisely. - A chirp-mass **proxy** $\tilde{\mathcal{M}}$ does two jobs: - **Heterodyning**: remove the leading-order chirp phase $\phi(f;\tilde{\mathcal{M}})$ from the data → aggressive multibanding. - **Prior conditioning**: the network learns $q(\theta \mid d, \tilde{\mathcal{M}})$ for narrow priors around $\tilde{\mathcal{M}}$, and infers $\delta\mathcal{M} = \mathcal{M} - \tilde{\mathcal{M}}$. - $\tilde{\mathcal{M}}$ is set per event: from a search trigger, or by a **chirp-mass scan** of the data. Then one network pass, with density → importance sampling. - Dax et al., [arXiv:2407.09602](https://arxiv.org/abs/2407.09602); worked example in the docs. ::: ::: {} ::: {.panel} [examples/binary_neutron_stars/train_settings.yaml]{.filetab .s-data} ::: {.darcula .sm} ```yaml data: ... chirp_prior_conditioning: kernel: chirp_mass: bilby.core.prior.Uniform(minimum=-0.005,… inference_parameters: [delta_chirp_mass, mass_ratio, ...] ``` ::: ::: ::: {.panel style="margin-top: 28px;"} [examples/binary_neutron_stars/GW170817.ini [(excerpt)]{.note}]{.filetab} ::: {.darcula .sm} ```ini fixed-context-parameters = {chirp_mass_proxy: 1.19786} # chirp-mass-scan = true ``` ::: ::: ::: {.procedure} [Chirp-mass scan (`chirp-mass-scan = true`)]{.head} 1. Sweep $\tilde{\mathcal{M}}$ over the training prior, on a grid set by the kernel width. 2. Draw a few samples per grid point (batched network passes). 3. Evaluate a phase-marginalized likelihood; the max-likelihood $\mathcal{M}$ is the trigger. About a minute of CPU time for a GW170817-like event. ::: ::: ::: ::: ## Recent developments [Multi-GPU training]{.sub} ::: {.body} ::: {.grid2} ::: {} - Distributed data parallel (DDP) training: set `num_gpus` in local settings. - `batch_size` and `num_workers` are totals, split across GPUs. - Requires `freeze_rb_layer: False` (the SVD-initialized first layer is trained) in all stages; `norm: LayerNorm` is recommended. - Optional `torch_compile` for the flow network. ::: ::: {.panel} [examples/dingo_t1/train_settings.yaml]{.filetab .s-local} ::: {.darcula .sm} ```yaml local: device: cuda num_gpus: 8 num_workers: 64 runtime_limits: max_time_per_run: 1_000_000 max_epochs_per_run: 500 checkpoint_epochs: 25 local_cache_path: /tmp ``` ::: ::: ::: ::: ## Recent developments [Further additions]{.sub} ::: {.body .center .large} - **Importance sampling**: synthetic $(\phi_c, \psi)$, calibration sampled in the same chain, cached likelihoods, rejection sampling. - **dingo_pipe**: injections, reproducible sampling seeds. - **Waveforms and detectors**: tidal models (NRTidal), SEOBNRv5PHM antisymmetric modes, triangular detectors. ::: ## Interactive tutorial []{.sub style="font-size: 38px;"} ::: {.body} ::: {.grid2 .wide-left} ::: {} | Notebook section | Key step | |:--|:--| | 1. Waveform dataset | [Generate training datasets]{.green} | | 2. Noise (ASD) dataset | [Generate training datasets]{.green} | | 3. Training a toy model | [Train the network]{.orange} | | 4. Injections (Sampler API) | [Perform inference]{.sblue} | | 5. GW150914 with `dingo_pipe` | [Perform inference]{.sblue} | | 6. The full run takes ~25 min on a laptop CPU. ::: ::: {} ![](images/tutorial_qr.svg){width=400 style="margin-top: 20px;"} ::: ::: ::: ## Extra Slides {visibility="hidden"} ::: {.absolute top=440 left=100 .big-title} Extra Slides ::: ## Training {visibility="hidden"} [Data settings]{.sub} ::: {.body} ::: {.grid2} ::: {} - Points to the waveform dataset - Specifies settings needed to generate simulated strain data: - data conditioning settings - detector configuration - extrinsic prior - reference time ([Dingo]{.sc} holds the Earth fixed) - Also takes list of inference parameters. By omitting parameters that are in the prior, [Dingo]{.sc} marginalizes over them. ::: ::: {.panel} [examples/npe_model/train_settings.yaml]{.filetab .s-data} ::: {.darcula .sm} ```yaml data: waveform_dataset_path: training_data/waveform_dataset.hdf5 train_fraction: 0.95 domain_update: f_min: 20.0 f_max: 1024.0 svd_size_update: 200 detectors: [H1, L1] extrinsic_prior: # Sampled at train time dec: default ra: default geocent_time: bilby.core.prior.Uniform(minimum=-0.10, m… psi: default luminosity_distance: bilby.core.prior.Uniform(minimum=1… ref_time: 1126259462.391 inference_parameters: [chirp_mass, mass_ratio, chi_1, chi… theta_jn, dec, ra, geocent_time, luminosity_distance, psi] ``` ::: ::: ::: ::: ## Data pre-processing {visibility="hidden"} ![](images/keynote_slide21.png){.absolute top=0 left=0 width=1920 height=1080} ## Training {visibility="hidden"} ![](images/keynote_slide22.png){.absolute top=0 left=0 width=1920 height=1080} ## Training {visibility="hidden"} [Local settings]{.sub} ::: {.body} ::: {.grid2} ::: {} - Infrastructure settings (don't affect final model). - Big models require a GPU, but CPU training is supported for prototyping - Full GPU utilization requires sufficient workers for preprocessing. - Multi-GPU training with `num_gpus`. - Optional external logging with Weights & Biases - `runtime_limits` and `condor` are cluster-specific. ::: ::: {.panel} [examples/npe_model/train_settings.yaml]{.filetab .s-local} ::: {.darcula .sm} ```yaml local: device: cuda num_workers: 32 runtime_limits: max_time_per_run: 3600000 max_epochs_per_run: 500 checkpoint_epochs: 50 leave_waveforms_on_disk: True condor: num_cpus: 32 memory_cpus: 128000 memory_gpus: 8000 request_disk: 50GB ``` ::: ::: ::: :::
